question.text: What will be the nationwide wastewater detection category of RSV on December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the WastewaterSCAN wastewater national category of RSV at the [WastewaterSCAN Dashboard](https://data.wastewaterscan.org/) displayed by the site when checked by Metaculus on or after December 1, 2026.
question.fine_print:
If the category is Not Detected or Not Calculated (or functional equivalent), the question resolves as Other. In case of accessibility issues with the main resolution source, Metaculus may check the [monthly update](https://wwscan.ghost.io/) as a backup source. In case of changes to categorization, the question may resolve based on which third of the current categories the new category falls into. For example, a new category of Very Low would be in the lower third and would be encompassed by the current Low category.

Please note that this question resolves solely according to what the dashboard displays at the time Metaculus checks it, regardless of subsequent revisions to it, revisions to historical data, reporting delays, or the accuracy of the displayed category.

# RSV national wastewater category (WastewaterSCAN) on 2026-12-01: research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: The dashboard is a JavaScript page, and the national RSV tile did not load when I fetched it, so I couldn't read the live value directly. [dashboard](https://data.wastewaterscan.org/)
- 2026-11-02: The October 2026 monthly update (data through Oct 31) says: "RSV is in the 'LOW' Wastewater Category due to not being in seasonal onset." RSV was detected in about 18% of October samples, up from about 9% in September. The median concentration was below the limit of detection, most sites show consistent non-detects, and detections are starting to rise in the South. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-october-2026-update/)
- How categories work: they combine three things: the 21-day trend, levels compared with national tertiles over the past 365 days, and how often the virus is detected. RSV is treated as a "seasonal" pathogen. In past newsletters, the national RSV category follows whether sites are in seasonal onset. HIGH was tied to ">50% of sites in seasonal onset." I found no published threshold for MEDIUM. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-december-2025-update/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-22: WastewaterSCAN's weekly Bluesky updates listed RSV as "Low" nationally. HMPV and Influenza B were also Low. SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and EV-D68 were High. [lightnews mirror](https://oauth.lightnews.app/bsky/wastewaterscan.bsky.social)
- 2026-08-13 through 2026-10-29: Every weekly update I found listed RSV as Low.
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The current category is Low and the season has not started nationally.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: German outlets report RSV, flu and pertussis rising in Bavaria. This is not US data. [Augsburger Allgemeine](https://www.augsburger-allgemeine.de/bayern/rsv-in-bayern-wie-viele-rs-viren-sind-aktuell-im-abwasser-9-115537876)
- 2026-11-02: WastewaterSCAN says it "remains to be seen" how the 2026-27 RSV season will go, and that 2025-26 started more slowly than 2024-25. In the same update, Influenza A was HIGH with an earlier-than-usual start. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-october-2026-update/)
- 2026-10-30: The CDC NWSS RSV page was updated, but the national value did not load for me. The page notes a data gap of about 200 sites because of a new testing contract. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/nwss/rv/RSV-national-data.html)

## 4. Base rates
- 2025 season: The national category was Low all through November 2025, including the Nov 25 weekly post, which said 6% of plants were in onset. [search summary of Bluesky mirrors](https://www.bushdrum.com/bsky/wastewaterscan.bsky.social)
- 2025-12-05: The November 2025 update (data through Nov 30) said RSV was LOW nationally, with "all sites in seasonal offset." Detection was about 34% of samples, and site categories were 115 Low, 2 Medium, 15 High. So on Dec 1, 2025 the national category was Low. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-november-2025-update/)
- 2026-01-08: By December 31, 2025, RSV was HIGH nationally, with detection at about 69% and more than 50% of sites in onset. That means it moved from Low to High within December 2025. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wastewaterscan-december-2025-update/)
- 2024 season: WastewaterSCAN says the network reached seasonal onset in "early December 2024," with a peak in early January 2025. I could not confirm the exact category shown on Dec 1, 2024.
- 2024-09-27: RSV was Low nationally and in all regions, with a modest rise in the South. [threadreader](https://threadreaderapp.com/user/WastewaterSCAN)
- 2023 season: I could not find the national category for early December 2023.
- 2026 compared with 2025: October detection was about 18% in 2026. For comparison, 2025 reached about 34% for November as a whole. I did not find an October 2025 detection rate, so I can't make a like-for-like comparison.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied (AI model releases, vaccines, weather, coral bleaching and others) relate to this question.
- I found no Metaculus community forecast and no expert forecast specifically on the WastewaterSCAN RSV category.
- There is a related method: a medRxiv preprint (2026) proposes an early-warning index for RSV built on WastewaterSCAN data. It does not give a 2026 forecast. [medRxiv](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.01.20.26344452.full.pdf)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- WastewaterSCAN posts weekly national updates on Bluesky, usually late in the week: around Nov 6, 13, 20 and 27. Those posts will show whether RSV goes past Low.
- CDC NWSS updates RSV wastewater levels each Friday. Watch for the national level moving out of "Very Low" or "Low"; the 200-site gap may affect it. [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/nwss/rv/RSV-national-data.html)
- Thanksgiving travel is around Nov 26. The dashboard depends on sampling and lab turnaround, so holiday reporting delays could affect what it shows on Dec 1. There were holiday data gaps in September 2026.
- The November 2026 monthly update will probably come out in early December, after the question resolves. It is only the backup source.
- Key uncertainty: in both recent seasons, onset came in early December. Whether the dashboard has moved past Low by Dec 1 depends on how fast the rise in the South spreads over the next 3-4 weeks.

- How the categories work, per the [about page](https://data.wastewaterscan.org/about/):
  - They combine trend, level and how often the virus is detected.
  - For RSV, a site is in "onset" or "offset" based on a 2,000 copies/g threshold, and offset is automatically LOW.

## 2. Current status

- **2024: borderline around December 1.**
  - 2024-11-22: LOW (data as of November 20), 22 sites in onset, about 44% detection over 3 weeks. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/nationwide-wwscan-november-2024-update-2/)

- **2023:** By 2023-12-13, all the Bay Area sites in that update were HIGH and in onset. I couldn't find the national category for December 1, 2023. [ghost](https://wwscan.ghost.io/scan-weekly-update-12-13-23/)

October 2026 detection (18%) is a bit above October 2025 (15.2%), and a newsletter said 2025 started "more slowly" than 2024.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction market prices you supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) relate to RSV or WastewaterSCAN.
- I found no Metaculus community forecast and no expert forecast of the WastewaterSCAN national RSV category.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly dashboard refreshes through November. The key signal is the share of sites in RSV onset, which needs to pass 50% for a national HIGH.
- The November 2026 monthly update will probably come out in early December, after Metaculus checks. Last year it was posted December 5.
- The CDC's weekly NWSS RSV wastewater data, published Fridays, is a cross-check. [CDC](https://cdc.gov/nwss/rv/RSV-statetrend.html)
- Thanksgiving (November 26) can bring sampling and reporting gaps. Under the about page's rules, a site with no sample in the last 7 days is flagged "Not Calculated."

(a) **Time left:** About 26 days. Resolution is whatever the dashboard shows on or after December 1, 2026. That display will likely reflect samples through about November 26-29, so Thanksgiving lab delays could matter.

(b) **Status quo:** Low. Every weekly WastewaterSCAN update from August 13 to October 29, 2026 listed RSV as Low nationally. The October monthly update says Low "due to not being in seasonal onset."

(c) **Base rates:**
- 2025: The national category was Low on December 1. All sites were in seasonal offset at November 30, and it jumped to High by December 31.
- 2024: Network-wide onset came in "early December." The December 1 category is unconfirmed, likely Low or near the transition.
- 2023: That season ran earlier, and the current onset-based categorization may not have existed yet.
- Overall: In the onset-based system, Low on December 1 is the more common outcome, but the transition usually happens in December. Timing within a week or two decides the answer.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **2026-11-02 (October update):** RSV detection was 18% of samples, up from 9% in September. The median concentration is still below the limit of detection, and detections are starting to rise in the South.
- **2026-10-29:** The weekly national category was Low.
- **2025-11-25:** Only 6% of plants were in onset, and the national category was still Low on December 1, 2025, despite 34% detection across November.
- **Earlier flu this year:** Influenza A is High with an earlier-than-usual start. This is weak evidence of an earlier respiratory season overall.
- **Category rule:** High requires more than 50% of sites in onset, a high bar to reach by late November. Medium has no published threshold and could be reached with a moderate share of sites in onset.

(e) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Medium or High:** The Southern rise spreads quickly through November, as in the earlier 2023-style seasons, and pushes many sites into onset by late November. That would yield Medium, or High if more than 50% of sites are in onset.
- **Other:** Holiday or contract disruptions lead to a "not calculated" display.

**Reasoning:** I started from roughly 65% Low, based on the status quo and the 2025 analog. I moved Low down by about 10 points for two reasons: October detection this year is already higher, and the early flu season suggests things may run somewhat earlier. I kept High below Medium because the more-than-50%-of-sites threshold is demanding for late November.
